category: mutable default argument shared across instances; cancellation state leaks between unrelated recurring events
issue: Cancelling a single occurrence of one recurring event wipes that date out of other, unrelated events. In one calendar the daily standup and a Friday retro both run from Monday 4 March 2024; cancelling the standup on Friday 8 March also makes the retro vanish from that day, and the retro was never touched. It is worse than that - any recurring event created after a cancellation is born already missing the cancelled date, so a brand new Mon/Wed/Fri series starting 4 March 2024 that should list 4, 6 and 8 March comes back as 4, 8 and 11 March. Cancellations passed in explicitly when the event is first set up behave correctly; it is only the ones applied afterwards that spread.

reference_fix.old:
def __init__(self, pattern, start, count=None, until=None, exclusions=[]):
        self.pattern = pattern
        self.start = start
        self.count = count
        self.until = until
        self.exclusions = exclusions
reference_fix.new:
def __init__(self, pattern, start, count=None, until=None, exclusions=None):
        self.pattern = pattern
        self.start = start
        self.count = count
        self.until = until
        self.exclusions = [] if exclusions is None else list(exclusions)
